label: Inline SQL++ call (from a JavaScript UDF)
type: embedding a SQL++ statement or expression directly as JavaScript syntax inside a UDF body, as against js-udf:n1ql-function-call's N1QL(stmt, params, opts) call form. Supports only named parameters (the N1QL() form supports both named and positional). Read-only - a data-changing statement must use n1ql:execute-function instead.
recurrence_note: 2 files, `divergent`, exactly at the promotion bar.
evidence: Calling SQL++ from the N1QL() function supports both named and positional parameters. Calling a SQL++ statement or expression inline supports only named parameters.

If you choose to use a SQL++ statement inside a JavaScript function, that function cannot have side effects that change data stored by Capella. Functions that change data must be called using the EXECUTE FUNCTION statement.
mustUseInsteadWhen: n1ql:execute-function (when the statement has side effects)
relates_to_competency_question: Are there two different ways to run SQL++ from inside a JavaScript UDF, and do they support the same parameter styles?
